summary: Plumas County lookout and radio station east of Quincy, begun 1938. Visitor accounts describe a communications site; firelookout.org lists it as gone, type ground.

facts.design: Temporary lookout and radio station, with a remote control link to the forest headquarters in Quincy (1938 plan)
facts.status_note: Visitor accounts describe a communications site. No source we read describes a lookout cab on the summit today. firelookout.org lists the site as gone, type ground, with no register number.

staffing.status: Harold Manson named in charge at construction in 1938; a May 1948 notice scheduled 21 lookout men for detection training at the station on June 1, 1948

visit.trail_note: Posts describe walking up from Quincy High School's switchback trail or from the bottom of Radio Hill Road.

events.note: Construction of a temporary lookout and radio station began in May 1938
Harold Manson named to be in charge of the station

May 29, 1948 notice: 21 Plumas lookout men to be called to the Radio Hill station on June 1 for detection training before manning their stations. This is a plan; no report that it took place was found.
General Services Administration declared the lookout site surplus (July 1973 announcement); the land included one acre with a building on it
Plumas County Board of Supervisors authorized an offer to purchase the site (November 29, 1973)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.org lists the site as gone (type ground). A 2024 visitor post and an undated visitor page describe a communications site and say the site was originally a fire lookout. We follow the visitor accounts for current use; no source we read describes a lookout cab there today.
An April 1938 item names a survey site on Cemetery Hill east of Quincy; the May 1938 items name Radio Hill. The clippings do not say whether they are the same place.

sources.title: The Daily Bucket: A hike on Radio Hill, Quincy, CA

notes_for_editor: Record says gone; firelookout.org says gone (type ground); visitor accounts describe a communications site and no lookout cab. The firelookout.org row for Radio Hill has no register number. An earlier draft's NHLR US 1153, CA 114 and Encl. Tower belong to Quartz Hill and were removed. The kind correction to enclosed_tower was withdrawn because firelookout.org lists Ground, which matches the current value. The 1948 call was a May 1948 plan, not a confirmed event. Ownership unverified: Peakbagging lists private land, and the 1973 county purchase was authorized but not confirmed as completed. Access level not recorded because no source states it. The 2024 Daily Kos post and the undated Idaho Alpine Zone page are personal accounts, not official records.
